content:
alex: Heads up — canary is showing a sustained compile-queue spike since the 2035000000 merge. +40% compile time and queue depth climbed across a few hosts.

mira: saw alerts. is this the kernel-selection change (PR #4218) that went out yesterday?

jonathan: yep that PR adjusted autotune score weighting (favours fewer kernels) — intended to reduce memory but I can revert if it's the culprit.

alex: quick telemetry: compile storm started ~10m after rollout, affected short-seq paths particularly. We also see KV cache invalidations around same time.

ci-bot: perf/regression job failed: benchmarks/short-seq-latency regressed 18% on canary (job 2035001240).

mira: can we get a small repro? logs show many `compile_request` retries with `cache_miss=true` and identical compile hashes.

jonathan: pasting snippet from one host:```
[13:21:02] compile_request kernel=attn_qkv_opt hash=0x7f1c
[13:21:02] cache_lookup miss key=kvcache:prefix:1234
[13:21:03] start_compile kernel=matmul_fused
[13:21:04] finish_compile id=xyz duration=420ms
[13:21:04] runtime: selected kernel=matmul_fused score=0.72 (expected attn_qkv_opt score=0.95)
```

sasha: that score inversion looks wrong. autotune scoring had a normalization step changed in the PR — could be a division by sequence length bug.

samir: also noticed the cache TTL computation was switched from seconds->ms in the same diff, so many entries are evicting immediately (hence repeated compiles).

lee: if TTL is effectively zero, kvcache misses cascade -> more compiles -> queue thrash. matches the telemetry.

alex: canary is currently rolled back? It's held — release pipeline blocked by product because some tenants saw SLO breaches. We need a hotfix or targeted revert ASAP.

jonathan: pushing small revert PR that restores old normalization and TTL units. will tag for rollback.

mira: before revert, can we run a quick branch build with unit test for scoring + an integration that mints a stable TTL value? I can run it on a debug pool.

jonathan: building now. attaching a debug build to canary-2 for 10% traffic to validate.

ci-bot: build 2035001248 started (job: runtime-autotune-smoke).

samir: also add a temporary guard: if TTL < 1000 then treat as 30s. quick hardening to stop immediate evictions in case of future unit errors.

alex: good call. sasha, can you own the rollout once build passes? coord with infra to scale compile workers down/up if needed.

sasha: on it. I'll monitor compile-queue and KV hit rate. alert thresholds lowered to catch regressions faster. :eyes:

mira: after hotfix, run a bisect to find the exact commit that introduced the scoring and TTL changes so we can add a test.

jonathan: will do a local bisect and open follow-up with unit tests for score normalization and TTL semantics.

alex: thanks team. keep this thread updated with canary metrics and CI outcomes.

lee: quick note: we should add a perf guard in CI that runs a short synthetic workload with KV caching to prevent this class of regression from merging unnoticed.

mira: adding an action item to runtime perf board.

alex: closing loop — if hotfix proves good by +10m and canary metrics return to baseline, we can unblock the release.

jonathan: build passed smoke tests; hotfix pushed to canary-2. monitoring.

sasha: initial metrics look promising — compile-queue down 60%, KV hit rate back to baseline. holding for 30m then escalate to prod rollback if stable. :thumbsup:
